name: Authomathics-MathCO-1000
description: Structured mathematical knowledge extraction from 1000 arXiv papers in combinatorics (math.CO). Each paper is parsed into a JSON file containing typed mathematical structures (definitions, theorems, lemmas, propositions, corollaries, conjectures, claims, problems, proofs, algorithms, tables) with assumption/conclusion splits, raw LaTeX, cleaned text, and cross-references. Extracted using the Authomathics rule-based parser with NtRED-distilled rules.

distribution.name: data-archive
distribution.description: Tar archive containing all parsed paper JSON files

distribution.name: paper-jsons
distribution.description: One JSON file per parsed arXiv paper, named {paper_id}_manual.json

recordSet.name: nodes
recordSet.description: Extracted mathematical structures from each paper

field.name: id
field.description: Structure identifier within paper (e.g., T1, L2, D3)

field.name: type
field.description: Structure type: definition, theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, conjecture, claim, problem, proof, algorithm, table

field.name: name
field.description: Optional name or attribution of the structure

field.name: raw_latex
field.description: Original LaTeX source of the structure

field.name: clean_text
field.description: LaTeX-stripped plain text with [MATH] placeholders for equations

field.name: assumptions
field.description: List of assumption clauses (theorem-like types only)

field.name: conclusions
field.description: List of conclusion clauses (theorem-like types only)

field.name: env_name
field.description: LaTeX environment name as found in source

field.name: index
field.description: Sequential index of the structure within its type in the paper

prov:wasGeneratedBy: Papers sourced from arXiv bulk data (math.CO category). LaTeX source files parsed programmatically using the Authomathics rule-based parser with NtRED-distilled rules. No human annotation was involved in the 1000-paper corpus; extraction is fully automated.
rai:dataCollectionType: Automated extraction from publicly available arXiv LaTeX sources.
rai:dataLimitations: The parser is rule-based and may miss non-standard LaTeX environments or custom theorem styles. Assumption/conclusion splitting relies on linguistic heuristics and may be imprecise for complex or unconventional mathematical phrasing. Coverage is limited to math.CO; generalization to other mathematical subfields is untested.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset reflects the conventions and topics of arXiv math.CO papers, which skew toward graph theory, enumerative combinatorics, and algebraic combinatorics. Author demographics and institutional representation are not balanced. English-language papers only.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal or sensitive information. The dataset contains only mathematical content extracted from publicly available arXiv papers. Author names appear only as part of theorem attributions within the mathematical text.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended for: (1) evaluating math structure extraction systems, (2) training/fine-tuning models for mathematical information extraction, (3) constructing mathematical knowledge graphs, (4) studying the structure and conventions of mathematical writing.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Positive: enables large-scale computational study of mathematical literature and supports open science. Negative risks are minimal as the data is purely mathematical content from public sources.
rai:hasSyntheticData: No. All content is extracted from real human-authored arXiv papers. The extraction process is deterministic (rule-based), but the underlying content is not synthetic.
